ko.executive_summary: SK Hynix and Samsung are aggressively expanding headcount to capture AI chip demand growth, while Tesla Terafab enters DRAM manufacturing and AMD recruits for GPU optimization. Industry-wide talent acquisition reflects intensifying competition for HPC and memory solutions.
key_facts: SK Hynix: Added 2,000+ jobs amid broader Korean hiring slowdown
Samsung: Stepping up US hiring ahead of Texas chip plants launch
Tesla Terafab: Hiring for DRAM chip manufacturing entry
AMD: Recruiting CPU engineer for GPU driver optimization
SK Hynix: Introducing half-day in-depth interviews and AI-centric hiring; eliminating education requirement for new talent

implications.text: SK Hynix and Samsung's concurrent hiring surges indicate critical race to secure AI chip production capacity and talent before demand peaks.
Tesla Terafab's DRAM entry signals diversification away from third-party memory suppliers and challenges established DRAM vendors' market share.
SK Hynix's elimination of education barriers and AI-centric recruitment reflects industry shift toward practical competency over credentials in HPC roles.

ko.counterpoint: US hiring momentum depends on Texas fab ramp timeline and potential regulatory delays.

ko.executive_summary: Broadcom and Marvell are gaining market traction on custom AI chip demand from hyperscalers, with Broadcom recording $30 billion in AI chip bookings and Marvell posting 42% data centre revenue growth. Custom silicon is reshaping competitive dynamics away from dominant GPU players.
key_facts: Broadcom: $30 billion in AI chip bookings; 40% stock rally
Marvell: 42% data centre revenue growth; custom AI chips landing at hyperscalers
Both companies outperforming NVIDIA over recent periods (36–40% gains)

implications.text: Large cloud operators are increasingly adopting custom ASICs to reduce GPU dependency and lower TCO, validating architectural diversification away from general-purpose accelerators.

implications.keyword: Market share pressure on GPU incumbents
implications.text: Broadcom and Marvell gains suggest NVIDIA's monopoly position in AI compute is eroding as customers invest in tailored solutions for specific workloads.

ko.counterpoint: Custom chip adoption remains concentrated among top-tier hyperscalers; demand concentration risk persists.

ko.executive_summary: Intel Foundry has landed a major new client, positioning itself as credible foundry alternative, while TSMC is expanding CoWoS packaging and reviving Longtan for 1.4nm capacity. Power semiconductors for AI datacenters are emerging as a critical growth segment alongside advanced packaging and silicon photonics adoption.
key_facts: Intel Foundry: Secured major unnamed client
TSMC: Reviving Longtan facility for 1.4nm fabs and CoWoS hub globally sold out
Infineon: Expanding AI datacenter power semiconductor production capacity
Silicon photonics and co-packaged optics (CPO): Gaining traction in AI datacenter interconnects to address power and signal integrity limits
Samsung: Pivoting research focus via GRO program to Physical AI, AI system architecture, and human-machine interfaces

implications.text: Intel's new major client win signals customer confidence in alternative nodes, reducing TSMC's single-source risk and lowering barriers to multi-foundry strategies.
AI datacenter power consumption scaling beyond GPU supply creates new opportunity in power semiconductors and thermal management as critical path items.
Silicon photonics and CPO adoption addresses copper signal degradation at hyperscale, enabling denser chiplet integration and lower power opex in AI infrastructure.
Shift from process-centric to Physical AI research signals Samsung's intent to capture post-Moore's law value in AI-optimized architectures and sensor-integrated systems.

ko.counterpoint: Intel foundry scale remains unproven at volume; Longtan revival timing faces geopolitical and supply chain execution risks.

ko.executive_summary: TSMC's CoWoS globally sold out and Longtan revival, Ajinomoto's advanced ABF demand surge, and industry focus on tiered memory and zHBM at FMS 2026 underscore packaging as critical AI memory and chiplet integration enabler. Cleanroom infrastructure capex is tracking toward significant growth through 2035.
key_facts: TSMC: CoWoS capacity fully sold out globally; Longtan revival for 1.4nm fabs and CoWoS hub
FMS 2026: Focus on tiered memory, zHBM, and advanced packaging
Ajinomoto: Riding advanced packaging demand surge via ABF material supply
Cleanroom equipment market: Projected to reach 190 Index by 2035 on fab capex

implications.text: TSMC CoWoS sell-out signals packaging capacity is now primary bottleneck in chiplet integration for AI memory (HBM, zHBM) and GPU-accelerator stacks.
Ajinomoto ABF demand growth reflects rapid scaling of chiplet interconnect substrates; material suppliers are now strategic chokepoints in packaging expansion.
FMS 2026 focus on tiered and zoned HBM signals industry-wide transition to disaggregated memory hierarchies, requiring advanced package-level integration.

ko.counterpoint: Packaging capex cycles lag fab construction; Longtan startup timeline and geopolitical supply constraints may delay CoWoS capacity relief.
